 Criminal Writ Petition No. 455 of 2023
 With
 Compounding Application Ia No.1 of 2023
Banti Kumar and Others ......Petitioners
 Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ..... Respondents
Mr. Girish Chandra Lakhchaura, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, Advocate for the respondent no.3.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

The petitioners Banti Kumar, Deepak Jha @ Jai Prakash, Manish Kumar and Sachin Dahiya @
Nipun seek quashing of the FIR No.28 of 2023, dated 21.01.2023, under Sections 419, 420, 406,
120-B and 411 IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District- Dehradun, on the basis of amicable settlement between the parties.
A joint compounding application has been filed along with the affidavits.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
It is a case of causing loss to a delivery agency by the delivery boys by changing the articles meant for delivery.
A statement is given that petitioner nos. 1 and 2 are in jail.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that two of the co-accused have already compounded offence in separate proceedings.

Reference has been made to WPCRL No.324 of 2023 and WPCRL No.420 of 2023, which relates to the instant FIR and those two cases have been decided on the basis of amicable settlement between the parties.
5. The petitioner nos. 3 and 4 are present in person before the Court.
The respondent no.3
joined the proceedings through video conferencing.
They are identified by their respective counsel.
They have accepted the compromise.

sentences.text: The Court particularly asked the respondent no. 3.
He would submit that the petitioners have compensated the company for the loss, which was caused by the petitioners.
7. Having considered all the attending factors, this Court is of the view that it is a case, which may be decided on the basis of amicable settlement between the parties.
Accordingly, the petition deserves to be allowed.
8. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
The FIR No.28 of 2023, dated 21.01.2023, under Sections 419, 420, 406, 120-B and 411 IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District- Dehradun, is hereby quashed.
9. The petitioner nos. 1 and 2 are in jail.
They be released forthwith, if not wanted in any other case.
10. Compounding Application No. 01 of 2023 stands disposed of, accordingly.
(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 23.03.2023
